methodology.finding: Drop rule 8.2's runner-up clause is applied on the 8-fund shortlist (2 survivors). On the 33-fund long list there are 5 survivors besides GLD (IAU, SGOL, SIVR, SLV, IGE), so under that reading the six dropped funds may not remain even as runners-up. Either way the surviving sleeve is precious metals only.

Inflation-beta conclusions are not robust. Gold's negative beta flips sign when CPI is paired with its release month (IAU IS +2.04) and no definition gives |t| above 1.65; SLV's beta is positive (IS +1.04), so 'gold and silver have negative inflation betas' is wrong for silver. The defensible statement is 'no detectable monthly relationship'; gold's -11% in 2022 and its real-yield sensitivity (OOS slope -8.0, t -4.4) are the stronger evidence.

The gold real-yield model has negative historical skill (corr -0.55 between prediction and realised 7y GLD CAGR, mean under-prediction 3.0 pts, overlapping windows) and broke OOS. Averaging 0.6% and 10.0% into 5.3% hides that neither is reliable; show the range.

Rank-test p-values are overstated by near-duplicates (8 TIPS funds, 3 gold clones, 4 precious baskets). On 13 category means: in-sample Sharpe vs OOS Sharpe -0.55 (p 0.052, not 0.0003); fundamental score vs OOS Sharpe +0.65 (p 0.017, survives); composite vs OOS Sharpe +0.21 (p 0.49). IAU/SGOL fee-artefact IRs vs GLD (0.51/0.47) sit in other_control.csv; removing them cuts composite vs OOS IR from +0.25 to +0.12.

methodology.finding: GSG roll assumption -1% is optimistic: its history implies about -5.5%/yr of roll plus real-spot drag (cannot be split: no GSCI spot series). The WIP model is nominal yields on 26% of the fund. SCHP's fund-yield method is backward-looking CPI accrual.
US_CPI has no 2025-10 print; inflation_beta and cpi_plus drop NaN before diff/pct_change, so the 2025-11 observation is a two-month change counted as one month.
Deflated Sharpe with V = 1/(T-1) is conservative here; the measured variance of the 32 OOS Sharpes gives IAU 0.69 (vs 0.46). Neither is near 0.95.

The in-sample fundamental score's cost component and the AUM hard screen use today's values (flagged in other_scored.csv); funds closed after 2017 are absent (survivorship). The composite itself uses only in-sample columns.
Memo 'How to explain' sentences match the JSON for all 8 (they are generated from it). The ROLE strings are hard-coded and overclaim inflation protection for IAU, WIP and IGF.
